admission.justification: Future language/anchor extensions must either supply a supported grammar with uniquely resolvable symbols or retain the language-independent line_range route. They cannot make an unsupported symbol valid by renaming the error; consumers must keep an actual resolvable locator.

alternatives.option: Refuse a symbol where no grammar exists and offer the language-independent line_range locator.
alternatives.reason: The appendix retains this boundary for other languages and supplies an actual locator rather than inventing a definition.

alternatives.option: Accept the requested symbol despite having no supported grammar.
alternatives.reason: The appendix retains this boundary for other languages and supplies an actual locator rather than inventing a definition.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Only if the owning approved requirement is explicitly revised to authorize this changed boundary; this prose is not a computed trigger.

consequences: Keep the explicit unsupported-language symbol refusal and the line_range alternative; changing grammar support requires an intentional implemented extension.
Rejected unsafe behavior is retained as a boundary, not promoted to a plausible serious alternative; no new implementation, execution or independent acceptance is asserted.
